To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a process is described to map the connections of specific neuron types across the whole mouse cortex and subcortical regions, registered to a standard reference atlas.
a process for whole brain reconstruction and registration of mouse brain sections labeled for standard histochemical techniques is described.
the whole mouse brain reconstruction and reference atlas registration workflow described here can be used to map the axon projections of specific neuron populations and the inputs to those neurons.

understanding how brain circuits are organized to support behavior.
understanding how brain circuits are organized and function in health and disease, with a focus on the role of specific cell types in the brain.
the development and application of new technologies for mapping neural circuitry in the mouse brain.

we have developed an image‐based approach to quantify axonal projections and inputs to a given neuron type in whole brain, and we have applied this method to a variety of mouse models.

The main takeaway from our work is that

standard histochemical processing can be used for high‐resolution mapping of neural circuits, which can be analyzed using the tools described here to generate whole‐brain maps of neuronal connectivity.

standard histochemical processing can be applied to whole mouse brains and registered to a reference brain atlas, allowing for quantitative analysis of neuronal projections and inputs across the whole mouse cortex.
standard histochemical techniques can be combined with modern image analysis techniques to provide quantitative maps of neuronal connectivity across the whole mouse forebrain.
